chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abu Ahmad Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Isa al-Jaludi al-Basri told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh told me, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Dhaheer told us, from al-Sanadi, from Abu Malik.
Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.' He said: Yasin is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family), and we are the Family of Yasin.

key_terms.يَاسِينَ: Yasin (interpreted here as a name/title for the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Family of Yasin' mentioned in the Quran according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith presents a specific exegetical view linking the Quranic phrase 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin' (Surah As-Saffat, 37:130) directly to the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt. It interprets 'Yasin' not merely as a divine name or surah title, but as a specific appellation for the Prophet, thereby establishing his family as the recipients of this divine salutation. This interpretation underscores the elevated spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt within Shia scholarly tradition.
